items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The API types are well named and documented (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashRegexRewrite, etc.), with doc comments on every field. The code follows the repo's existing file-per-feature layout (consistent_hash.go, consistent_hash_test.go). Commit message and final summary are clear.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The feature lives in its own consistent_hash.go and follows the plugin pattern: IR, construct, apply, merge. Deepcopy and CRD come from `make go-generate-apis`. The final hash list is built once, so apply just assigns `action.HashPolicy = consistentHash.hashPolicies`. Unit tests and golden tests were added. No debug leftovers.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The CRD caps list sizes (MaxItems=16) and string lengths, and a Pattern restricts ttl to a Go duration or whole seconds. A bad ttl or regex is reported as an error on the policy rather than dropped silently. Apply returns early when the IR is nil. A test checks that merging doesn't change p2's source state.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: The golden test with full + secondary policies shows the union with the primary's entries first, dedup, and re-sorting (headers…sourceIp). Merge metadata lists both policies under `consistentHash`. The summary says sourceIp is kept from the higher-priority policy even when unset. Hidden F2P tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: Golden output for `{}` is a single `connectionProperties: sourceIp: true` with no terminal. There is a disable golden test. The CEL rule `!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (!has(self.headers)...)` is on ConsistentHash and was generated into the CRD.
